top_stories.title: Birsa Munda: His legacy, Ulgulan and the Adivasi identity debate
top_stories.rephrased_article: On June 9th, tribal organizations in Jharkhand pledged to protect the legacy of **Birsa Munda**, an iconic Adivasi leader who fought against colonial rule and land encroachment.  **Amit Shah**, the Union Home Minister, was involved in a recent demand for delisting Christian converts from the Scheduled Tribes (ST) list, reigniting debate over Adivasi identity.  **Birsa Munda**, born in 1875, became known as "Dharti Aba," leading the Ulgulan movement against colonial rule and non-tribal landlords. His influence extended beyond Jharkhand to other states, making him a central figure in debates about Adivasi rights, land ownership, religion, and self-governance.  He died in 1900 after being arrested for inciting resistance against British authority and Christian missionaries.

top_stories.title: 40 years ago June 11, 1986: Army on alert in Haryana | The Indian Express
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Haryana** **government** has alerted the **army** to meet any situation following a report by the **Venkataramiah Commission**.  The government also requisitioned about 80 companies of paramilitary forces to help maintain peace. In Cape Town, violence between rival Black groups in a squatter camp resulted in five more deaths, bringing the total to ten. Meanwhile, Sikh extremists in Western Canada planned attacks on Expo-86 with rocket launchers and other weapons.

top_stories.title: Indians abroad sent home a record $110 billion. What it means for India's economy
top_stories.rephrased_article: **India's** record remittances of $110.47 billion in 2025-26 cushioned its finances, particularly during a period of weak foreign investment and capital outflows. The surge in remittances, driven by the West Asia conflict and the rupee's depreciation, helped offset the impact on the Balance of Payments (BoP). However, economists warn that relying solely on remittances for long-term economic stability is not feasible.  The government must focus on improving Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) inflows and managing the trade deficit to achieve sustainable growth.

top_stories.title: Asian stocks fall, oil gains as US strikes Iran - The Economic Times
top_stories.rephrased_article: **US** military strikes on **Iran** for a second consecutive day sent oil prices soaring, impacting global markets. The **MSCI’s** gauge for Asian equities dropped 1%, while tech stocks continued to decline as investors remained cautious following the geopolitical tensions.  The **Nasdaq 100 Index** fell 2% due to concerns over rising interest rates and a selloff in semiconductor companies. Gold prices also declined, reflecting fears of higher inflation. The US dollar strengthened against most Group-of-10 currencies, while Treasury futures fell as investors anticipated further volatility.

top_stories.title: War-wary, May equity MF inflows fall 40% to year low - The Economic Times
top_stories.rephrased_article: **MF industry** flows decreased in May, with SIPs reaching 30,954 crore, down slightly from April. **Investors** adopted a wait-and-watch approach due to global concerns and market volatility, leading to lower lump-sum investments.  While flexi-cap funds saw the highest inflows, other categories like small-cap and mid-cap funds experienced declines. Gold ETFs also saw outflows for the first time in 13 months, while debt mutual funds recorded net outflows. The industry saw a slowdown in new fund launches.

top_stories.title: 24-year-old PhD student spotted a strange signal from space and uncovered one of astronomy's greatest discoveries | - The Times of India
top_stories.rephrased_article: In 1967, **Jocelyn Bell Burnell**, a PhD student at the University of Cambridge, discovered pulsars while analyzing radio telescope data.  The unusual signal, repeating with precise regularity, was initially thought to be from extraterrestrial sources but eventually identified as originating from neutron stars, rapidly spinning remnants of dead stars. This discovery revolutionized astrophysics by providing evidence for the existence of these objects and opening new avenues for studying extreme conditions in the universe. While **Antony Hewish** and **Martin Ryle** received the Nobel Prize in Physics for their work on radio astronomy and pulsar discovery, Bell Burnell's contribution was not recognized at the time, sparking ongoing debate about scientific credit and recognition.  Despite this controversy, Bell Burnell has become a respected astronomer and her work continues to shape modern astrophysics.

top_stories.title: Bond traders keep bets on Fed hike in 2026 - The Economic Times
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Traders** are adjusting their expectations for interest rate hikes after the US core consumer price index (CPI) rose 0.2% in May, falling short of economist forecasts.  The **Federal Reserve** may now have more breathing room to wait and see before raising rates further, as bond traders maintain expectations for a December hike despite the softer inflation reading. The **US dollar** slipped while two-year Treasury yields decreased slightly.

top_stories.title: "Erica was described as an emotional asset": Candace Owens keeps pressure on officials over controversial Erika Kirk email - The Times of India
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Candace Owens** doubled down on her Freedom of Information Act request tied to an email mentioning **Erika Kirk**, claiming federal agencies are resisting her efforts. She accused media personality **Andrew Colvett** of advising others to lie about the authenticity of the leaked email and alleged that officials prioritized managing public reaction over safety concerns following the shooting incident. Owens argued that the response from government departments only strengthened her suspicions and she remains confident the document is authentic. The dispute surrounding the email's authenticity and the individuals involved continues to fuel online debate.

top_stories.title: Bond traders keep bets on Fed hike in 2026 - The Economic Times
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Traders** are adjusting their expectations for interest rate hikes after the US core consumer price index (CPI) rose 0.2% in May, falling short of economists' predictions. **The Federal Reserve** may now have more breathing room to wait and see before raising rates further, as the softer inflation reading eases immediate pressure on them.  Bond traders had previously priced in multiple rate hikes this year, but the recent CPI data suggests a "wait and see" approach is likely.

top_stories.title: Man Robbed Of Rs 1.5 Crore Cash At Gunpoint In Delhi: Cops
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Two employees** of a building material trader were robbed at gunpoint of Rs 1.5 crore in north Delhi's Sarai Rohilla area on Wednesday. The incident occurred near the Zakhira flyover as the two employees, traveling on a scooter with the cash, were intercepted by two unidentified men on a motorcycle.  The robbery was captured on CCTV cameras and police are examining the footage to identify and trace the robbers. A case has been registered at the Sarai Rohilla police station and multiple teams have been formed to conduct the probe.
